title: Sudarśana, the Lord of Time
body:
Sudarśana Jayanti celebrates Chakrattāzhwār, the Sudarśana Chakram of Sriman Nārāyaṇa, and his greatness.

In his Shōḍaśa Āyudha Stōtram, Swāmi Dēśikan reveals the nature of Sudarśana:

यदायत्तं जगच्चक्रं कालचक्रं च शाश्वतम् ।
पातु वस्तत्परं चक्रं चक्ररूपस्य चक्रिणः ॥

yadāyattaṁ jagaccakraṁ kālacakraṁ ca śāśvatam |
pātu vastat paraṁ cakraṁ cakrarūpasya cakriṇaḥ ||

Swāmi Dēśikan prays for the welfare of all, and asks the sixteen-armed Chakrattāzhwār to protect us. He speaks of time as the aspect of nature that moves eternally forward, and declares that time itself is governed by Sudarśana: the foremost weapon of the Lord, who is none other than the Lord Himself, manifest in the form of the Chakram.
